attributes.body_ja:
「のみならず」は、「だけ」と同（おな）じ意味（いみ）を持（も）つ文語（ぶんご）の助詞（じょし）「のみ」を含（ふく）む文法（ぶんぽう）で、これに五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「なる」の否定形（ひていけい）の語幹（ごかん）に文語（ぶんご）の助動詞（じょどうし）「ず」を付（つ）けたものです。「ず」は「ない」と同（おな）じように、動詞（どうし）と結（むす）びついて否定（ひてい）を表（あらわ）します。この表現（ひょうげん）は「(A) だけではなく (B) も」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

「のみ」は「だけ」と同（おな）じように、動詞（どうし）、イ形容詞（けいようし）、ナ形容詞（けいようし）、名詞（めいし）に接続（せつぞく）します。

「のみならず」は文（ぶん）の頭（あたま）に置（お）かれて接続詞（せつぞくし）として機能（きのう）することもあります。この場合（ばあい）も意味（いみ）は変（か）わりませんが、ニュアンスは「さらに」や「加（くわ）えて」に近（ちか）づきます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「のみならず」は硬（かた）い表現（ひょうげん）なので、主（おも）に文章（ぶんしょう）や、スピーチ・演説（えんぜつ）などで使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
のみならず is a structure consisting of のみ, the literary particle equivalent of だけ meaning 'just' or 'only', the negative stem-form of the う-Verb なる 'to be', and the literary auxiliary verb ず, which connects with verbs in the same way, and carries the same meaning as ない. This expression indicates that something is 'not just (A), but also (B)', or 'not only (A), but (B) too'.

のみ connects to words in the same way as だけ, so this pattern will be seen following Verbs, い-Adjectives, な-Adjectives, or nouns.

Occasionally, のみならず may function as a conjunction, appearing at the beginning of a new sentence. In these cases, the meaning is the same, but usually translates closer to 'what's more', 'furthermore', or 'moreover'.

Caution

As this structure is formal, it will primarily be seen in literature, or heard in speeches.

attributes.body: だけ conveys 'only' or 'just.' In contrast, のみならず is a formal expression similar to だけじゃなく, meaning 'not only A, but also B.' While だけ expresses limitation, のみならず emphasizes a lack of restriction. Note that while だけ is commonly used in both everyday speech and writing, のみならず is more formal and typically limited to written language or formal speech.

second_relatable.title: のみならず
second_relatable.meaning: Not only...but, Not just...but, What is more

attributes.body: Both mean not only…but also, but differ in register and nuance. に限らず stresses inclusiveness, as in 日本に限らず世界中で使われている (Used not only in Japan but worldwide). のみならず is more formal and often adds additional, sometimes surprising, information, as in 彼は日本語のみならず英語も話せる (He speaks not only Japanese but also English).

attributes.body: はもとより and のみならず both mean 'not only... but also'. はもとより is slightly more formal and can add the nuance of 'let alone' for the first part, emphasizing the inclusion of the second. のみならず is still formal but slightly less so, and puts more of the focus on the second thing being a noteworthy addition on top of the first.

attributes.body: ばかりでなく and のみならず are both expressions used to convey the meaning of 'Not only (A)'. While both are formal, のみならず is even more literary. Both patterns can also be followed by noun + も to express 'But also (B)'. For example, 日本語のみならず、韓国語も話せる 'He can speak not only Japanese, but also Korean.' vs. 日本語ばかりでなく、韓国語も話せる (Same meaning, but slightly less literary in tone).

attributes.body: のみならず and だけでなく(て)～も are nearly identical in meaning, both meaning 'Not only (A), but also (B)'. のみならず is by far the more formal expression, while だけでなく (especially in the alternate form だけじゃなくて) is more common in everyday speech. For example, 日本語のみならず、韓国語も話せる 'He can speak not only Japanese, but also Korean.' vs. 日本語だけじゃなくて、韓国語も話せる (Same meaning, but far more casual).

second_relatable.meaning: Not only ~ but ~ also, Not just ~ but ~ also

attributes.body: のみならず and だけでなく are essentially synonymous in that they both express non-exclusivity (i.e. 'not only'), but differ in formality. While だけでなく is common in both everyday speech (often appearing as だけじゃなくて) and writing, のみならず is a highly formal expression used primarily in writing and academic contexts. Both phrases are often followed by a noun + も to convey 'not only (A), but also (B)'.
